title: Positivity, invariant domains and entropy-stable systems fluxes

items.title: Convex invariant domains for a one-step update
items.statement:
Let $m,N\ge1$, let $\mathcal A\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be a state domain, and let
$\Phi:\mathcal A^N\to\mathcal A^N$ be a one-step update on $N$ cell states.
A set $K\subseteq\mathcal A$ is **convex** if
$\theta U+(1-\theta)V\in K$ for every $U,V\in K$ and $\theta\in[0,1]$.
It is a **convex invariant domain for $\Phi$** if it is convex and
$\Phi(K^N)\subseteq K^N$. The word invariant refers only to this stated
one-step map and its stated admissible inputs; it asserts no invariance for a
different flux, time integrator, or exact Riemann evolution.
items.strategy: Give the typed definition and exact scope; no preservation property is inferred for another map.

references.title: J.-L. Guermond and B. Popov, Invariant Domains and First-Order Continuous Finite Element Approximation for Hyperbolic Systems
references.locator: §2.2, Definitions 2.3–2.4, PDF pp. 3–4; complete 24-page article read

items.title: Convex entropy pairs, entropy variables, and entropy potentials for systems
items.statement:
Use the conservation-system convention of
[[def-hyperbolic-system-and-characteristic-families]]: on an open convex state
domain $\mathcal A\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, the flux is $F:\mathcal A\to\mathbb R^m$.
A **convex entropy pair** is a pair $(\eta,q)$ with $\eta\in C^2(\mathcal A)$,
$q\in C^1(\mathcal A)$, positive-semidefinite Hessian $D^2\eta$, and
$$Dq(U)=D\eta(U)\,DF(U)\qquad(U\in\mathcal A).$$
The **entropy variable** is the column vector $v(U)=\nabla\eta(U)$; gradients
are represented as columns, so the compatibility equation above means
$\nabla q(U)=DF(U)^T v(U)$. The **entropy potential** is
$\psi(U)=v(U)^T F(U)-q(U)$. This definition does not assert that every convex
$\eta$ admits a flux $q$; the compatibility equation is part of the hypothesis.
items.strategy: State derivative and column-vector conventions; no existence of q is asserted.

items.title: Maximal convex scaling toward an admissible cell mean
items.statement:
Let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be closed and convex (convex in the sense of
[[def-pe03-convex-invariant-domain]]), let $J$ be a finite nonempty
index set, let $w_j>0$ with $\sum_{j\in J}w_j=1$, and let input states
$V_j\in\mathbb R^m$ have mean $\bar V=\sum_jw_jV_j\in K$. The **maximal
convex scaling limiter** returns the largest $\theta\in[0,1]$ for which every
$$V_j^\theta=\bar V+\theta(V_j-\bar V)$$
belongs to $K$, together with all the states $V_j^\theta$. Equivalently, form
$$S=\{\theta\in[0,1]:V_j^\theta\in K\text{ for every }j\in J\},$$
and return $\theta_*:=\max S$ and $(V_j^{\theta_*})_{j\in J}$. The mean is
assumed admissible; implementation, cost, and any pointwise-in-cell property
are not part of this definition.
items.strategy: Specify the finite input, output, feasible set, and maximum selection; make no complexity claim.

items.title: First-order finite-volume update using supplied HLL speeds
items.statement:
Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathbb R^m$ be the flux of the one-dimensional system in
[[def-hyperbolic-system-and-characteristic-families]]. On a periodic uniform
mesh of $N\ge2$ cells of width $h>0$, let $U_i\in\mathcal A$ be the cell means
and put $\nu=\Delta t/h\ge0$. At each face $(i+1/2)$ choose explicit speeds
$S_{L,i+1/2}<0<S_{R,i+1/2}$ and evaluate the middle branch of the HLL flux
[[def-hll-two-wave-flux]] on $(U_i,U_{i+1})$. The **first-order HLL update** is
$$U_i^+=U_i-\nu\bigl(\widehat F_{i+1/2}-\widehat F_{i-1/2}\bigr),\qquad i\pmod N.$$
The speeds are supplied data. Neither this definition nor later algebraic
results assert that they enclose the wave speeds of an exact nonlinear Riemann
solution.
items.strategy: State the indexing, periodic convention, flux branch, and supplied-speed caveat.

items.title: Positive-margin admissible states for ideal-gas Euler
items.statement:
Fix $\gamma>1$ and $\varepsilon>0$, and use the state variables and internal
energy density from [[def-ideal-gas-euler-state-and-pressure]]. Define the
**positive-margin set**
$$K_{\gamma,\varepsilon}:=\left\{(\rho,m,E):\rho\ge\varepsilon,\quad E-\frac{m^2}{2\rho}\ge\varepsilon\right\}.$$
Every member has positive density and positive pressure. Closedness and
convexity are proved in
[[prop-pe03-euler-state-and-margin-domains-are-convex-and-closed]]; those properties are not
being inferred from this definition alone.
items.strategy: Define the set and defer its closedness and convexity to a proved proposition.

items.title: Ideal-gas Euler states remain positive under Lax–Friedrichs flux splitting
items.statement:
Fix $\gamma>1$. For $U=(\rho,m,E)\in\mathcal G_\gamma$, let
$e=E-m^2/(2\rho)$, $p=(\gamma-1)e$, $u=m/\rho$, and
$c=\sqrt{\gamma p/\rho}$. If $a\ge |u|+c$, then both split states
$$U_\delta=U+\delta F(U),\qquad \delta\in\{-1/a,1/a\},$$
belong to $\mathcal G_\gamma$, where $F(U)=(m,m^2/\rho+p,u(E+p))$.
More precisely, with $x=1+\delta u$ their density and internal-energy density are
$$\rho_\delta=\rho x,\qquad e_\delta=e x-\frac{\delta^2p^2}{2\rho x}>0.$$
items.strategy: Compute the split density and internal energy, then bound the exact pressure term using c^2=gamma p/rho.

items.title: Tadmor entropy-conservative two-point flux
items.statement:
Let $(\eta,q)$ be a convex entropy pair on an open domain $\mathcal A$, with
entropy variable $v$ and potential $\psi$ as in
[[def-pe03-system-entropy-pair-and-potential]]. A continuous two-point flux
$F^{ec}:\mathcal A\times\mathcal A\to\mathbb R^m$ is **entropy-conservative
in Tadmor's sense** if it is consistent and symmetric,
$F^{ec}(U,U)=F(U)$, and satisfies the exact jump identity
$$\bigl(v(U_R)-v(U_L)\bigr)^T F^{ec}(U_L,U_R)=\psi(U_R)-\psi(U_L)$$
for every pair $U_L,U_R\in\mathcal A$. This definition asserts no existence
for a prescribed entropy pair.
items.strategy: State consistency, symmetry, domain, and jump identity; do not claim existence.

items.title: Euler positive states are convex and positive-margin sets are closed convex
items.statement:
Fix $\gamma>1$ and $\varepsilon>0$. The ideal-gas admissible set
$$\mathcal G_\gamma=\left\{(\rho,m,E):\rho>0,\ E-\frac{m^2}{2\rho}>0\right\}$$
and the positive-margin set $K_{\gamma,\varepsilon}$ from
[[def-pe03-euler-positive-margin-domain]] are convex, and
$K_{\gamma,\varepsilon}$ is closed in $\mathbb R^3$.
items.strategy: Prove the kinetic-energy perspective inequality by weighted Cauchy–Schwarz and verify closedness by continuity away from rho=0.

items.title: Entropy-stable flux from positive-semidefinite entropy-variable dissipation
items.statement:
Let $(\eta,q)$ be an entropy pair with entropy variable $v$ and potential
$\psi$, and let $F^{ec}$ be a consistent entropy-conservative flux as in
[[def-pe03-tadmor-entropy-conservative-flux]]. For each pair
$(U_L,U_R)\in\mathcal A^2$, choose a symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix
$D(U_L,U_R)\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}$. The associated **entropy-stable
dissipative flux** is
$$F^{es}(U_L,U_R):=F^{ec}(U_L,U_R)-\frac12D(U_L,U_R)(v(U_R)-v(U_L)).$$
Positive semidefinite means $z^TD(U_L,U_R)z\ge0$ for every $z\in\mathbb R^m$.
No fully discrete time-step property is included.
items.strategy: State the matrix condition and exclude fully discrete conclusions.

items.title: First-order HLL updates are averages of adjacent half-cell fan averages
items.statement:
Use the first-order HLL update of
[[def-pe03-first-order-hll-finite-volume-update]]. At a face with left and right
states $U_L,U_R$, supplied speeds $S_L<0<S_R$, and physical flux values
$F_L=F(U_L),F_R=F(U_R)$, define
$$U_*:=\frac{S_RU_R-S_LU_L-(F_R-F_L)}{S_R-S_L}.$$
If the one-sided CFL bounds $2\nu(-S_L)\le1$ and $2\nu S_R\le1$ hold, the
averages of the HLL fan over the adjacent left and right half-cells are,
respectively,
$$A^-=(1-2\nu(-S_L))U_L+2\nu(-S_L)U_*,\qquad A^+=(1-2\nu S_R)U_R+2\nu S_RU_*.$$
For every cell $i$, the updated mean satisfies
$$U_i^+=\frac12\left(A^+_{i-1/2}+A^-_{i+1/2}\right),$$
where each face uses its own supplied speeds and intermediate state.
items.strategy: Derive the HLL flux identities algebraically, integrate the piecewise constant fan over half-cells, and substitute into the update.

items.title: First-order HLL update preserves a convex invariant domain under admissible fan averages
items.statement:
Let $K$ be a convex set in the state domain, and consider a periodic uniform
mesh and one first-order HLL update as defined in
[[def-pe03-first-order-hll-finite-volume-update]]. Assume every cell mean
$U_i\in K$. At every face impose the **HLL fan-average hypothesis** that the
two adjacent half-cell averages $A^-,A^+$ from
[[lem-pe03-hll-half-cell-riemann-averages]] lie in $K$, with that lemma's local
CFL bounds. Then every updated mean $U_i^+$ belongs to $K$. A sufficient
condition for the fan-average hypothesis is that every HLL intermediate state
$U_*\in K$, because the stated CFL makes each half-cell average a convex
combination of a cell state and $U_*$. The result does not assert a bound on
exact nonlinear wave speeds.
items.strategy: Show each HLL half-cell average is a convex combination, then average the two halves.

items.title: Semidiscrete cell entropy inequality for Tadmor-dissipative fluxes
items.statement:
Let $(\eta,q)$ be a convex entropy pair on an open set $\mathcal A$, with
entropy variable $v$ and potential $\psi$ as in
[[def-pe03-system-entropy-pair-and-potential]]. On a periodic mesh of $N\ge2$
cells of width $\Delta x>0$, let differentiable states $U_i(t)\in\mathcal A$
satisfy
$$\dot U_i=-\frac{F^{es}_{i+1/2}-F^{es}_{i-1/2}}{\Delta x},$$
where every face flux is the entropy-stable dissipative flux of
[[def-pe03-entropy-stable-dissipative-flux]]. Define
$$\widehat q_{i+1/2}:=\left(\frac{v_i+v_{i+1}}2\right)^T F^{es}_{i+1/2}-\frac{\psi_i+\psi_{i+1}}2.$$
Then each cell satisfies
$$\frac{d}{dt}\eta(U_i)+\frac{\widehat q_{i+1/2}-\widehat q_{i-1/2}}{\Delta x}\le0.$$
Summing over the periodic mesh gives nonincrease of total discrete entropy.
This is a semidiscrete result; it asserts no entropy inequality for a chosen
fully discrete time integrator.
items.strategy: Compute the face jump defect, derive the consistent numerical entropy flux, and combine the two face contributions in each cell.

items.title: Convex scaling preserves the cell mean and positive-margin node states
items.statement:
Fix $\gamma>1$, $\varepsilon>0$, a finite nonempty node set $J$, positive
weights $w_j$ summing to one, and candidate states $V_j\in\mathbb R^3$ with
mean $\bar V=\sum_jw_jV_j\in K_{\gamma,\varepsilon}$. Apply the maximal
convex scaling limiter of
[[alg-pe03-convex-scaling-positivity-limiter]] with $K=K_{\gamma,\varepsilon}$.
Its output is well-defined, every limited node lies in $K_{\gamma,\varepsilon}$,
and the weighted cell mean remains $\bar V$. Hence every limited node has
positive density and positive pressure. If the unscaled nodes already lie in
$K_{\gamma,\varepsilon}$, the maximal parameter is $\theta_*=1$. In
particular, if smooth target states stay a distance at least $\delta>0$ from
$\mathbb R^3\setminus K_{\gamma,\varepsilon}$ and each reconstruction node
has error less than $\delta$, the limiter is inactive and preserves that
reconstruction's accuracy. No positivity between finitely many nodes is
claimed.
items.strategy: Use compactness of the closed feasible-parameter set, compute the weighted mean, and prove the strict-margin inactivity condition.

items.title: Symmetric HLL speeds preserve ideal-gas density and internal-energy positivity
items.statement:
Fix $\gamma>1$ and a periodic uniform mesh. Suppose every cell state
$U_i\in\mathcal G_\gamma$. Apply the first-order HLL update of
[[def-pe03-first-order-hll-finite-volume-update]]. At each face $(i+1/2)$ choose a symmetric HLL
branch $S_L=-a_{i+1/2}$, $S_R=a_{i+1/2}$ with
$$a_{i+1/2}\ge\max\bigl(|u_i|+c_i,|u_{i+1}|+c_{i+1}\bigr),\qquad 2\nu a_{i+1/2}\le1.$$
Then one first-order HLL update preserves $\mathcal G_\gamma$; in particular,
every updated density and pressure is strictly positive. This is the symmetric
local Lax–Friedrichs branch with a stated speed bound, not a claim that arbitrary
HLL speed estimates are valid or that the bound is necessary.
items.strategy: Prove both Lax–Friedrichs split states are admissible, express the HLL middle state as their convex average, and invoke the invariant-domain update theorem.

title: Positivity, invariant domains and entropy-stable systems fluxes — Examples

items.title: Exact Tadmor entropy residual for a dissipative Burgers flux
items.statement:
For Burgers' flux $f(u)=u^2/2$ and entropy $\eta(u)=u^2/2$, the entropy flux
is $q(u)=u^3/3$ and the entropy potential is $\psi(u)=u^3/6$. The symmetric
two-point flux
$$f^{ec}(u_L,u_R)=\frac{u_L^2+u_Lu_R+u_R^2}{6}$$
is entropy-conservative. Adding unit dissipation in entropy variables gives
$f^{es}=f^{ec}-(u_R-u_L)/2$; at the jump $1\to0$ its Tadmor entropy residual
is exactly $-1/2$.
items.strategy: Verify entropy compatibility and factor the cubic jump exactly.

items.title: Two Euler quadrature nodes rescaled to a positive margin
items.statement:
With weights $w_1=w_2=1/2$, cell mean $\bar U=(1,0,1)$, and candidate
conserved states $V_1=(1,4,1)$ and $V_2=(1,-4,1)$, apply the limiter to
$K_{7/5,1/2}$. It returns $\theta_*=1/4$, giving states $(1,1,1)$ and
$(1,-1,1)$ with positive pressure and the original cell mean.
items.strategy: Compute the internal energy along the scaling segment and check the mean directly.

items.title: An entropy-stable Burgers flux still smears an under-resolved shock
items.statement:
For the Burgers flux and quadratic entropy, the unit-dissipation
entropy-stable flux has a negative Tadmor residual at the entropy shock
$1\to0$. On the four-cell
periodic data $(1,1,0,0)$ and with $\nu=\Delta t/\Delta x=1/2$, one explicit
forward-Euler update replaces the two states adjacent to that jump by
$11/12$ and $1/3$. Thus semidiscrete entropy stability coexists with visible
shock smearing at this coarse resolution. This computation gives no
fully-discrete entropy inequality for forward Euler.
items.strategy: Verify the shock entropy sign, the numerical fluxes, the semidiscrete residual, and the explicit finite update separately.

items.title: A near-vacuum Euler state remains positive under symmetric HLL speeds
items.statement:
Take $\gamma=7/5$, density $\rho=10^{-8}$, pressure $p=10^{-12}$, and
velocities $u_L=-1/100$, $u_R=1/100$. The conserved states have
$m_{L,R}=\mp10^{-10}$ and $E_{L,R}=3\times10^{-12}$. Choose the symmetric HLL
speed $a=11/500$ at every face and Courant ratio $\nu=\Delta t/h=125/11$.
For the four-cell periodic data $(U_L,U_L,U_R,U_R)$, one HLL forward-Euler
update preserves positive density and pressure despite the very small initial
values. The calculation illustrates a first-order positivity branch; it does
not claim accuracy of the shock profile.
items.strategy: Verify the Euler states, sound speed, speed branch, CFL, and convex update coefficients exactly.
